name: Turn a synth tom-style epic drum hit into a distant low explosion / drop boom: harmonic bass enhance plus an octave-down sub, a 6 dB/oct low-pass instead of an attack boost, reverb low-cut around 100 Hz at 24 dB/oct, a band-limited quarter-note delay with about 7 ms early/late L/R offsets, a parallel tremolo or auto-pan tail whose depth is faded in by a delayed envelope, and an optional low comb filter (about 14-40 Hz) for a modern metallic drop
goal: Make a far-away 'whoa, what happened' cinematic boom for drops and section hits, starting from a synthesized drum hit (see the epic hybrid drum / taiko-from-noise skills for building the hit itself). This skill adds the distance, sub and tail processing: a rumbling, darker boom with a moving stereo tail.
prerequisites: A synthesized drum hit (noise + oscillator with fast pitch/filter envelopes) or a tom sample
EQ with selectable slopes, a bass enhancer / sub generator, convolution reverb, a delay with per-side offset, a tremolo and auto-pan with modulatable depth, a comb filter
A parallel bus or split-lane routing

inputs.name: hit
inputs.description: Source epic drum / tom hit, played low on the keyboard

inputs.name: tempo
inputs.description: Song BPM for syncing delay and tremolo

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.

Vendor plugins named in the video (an all-in-one synth, a bass enhancer, free modulation effects) are mapped to generic EQ, sub-harmonic, reverb, delay, tremolo, auto-pan and comb modules. Without a split-lane synth, use a parallel bus and blend by fader.
Watch the gain while you work: sub enhancement, delay and comb feedback each push the level up quickly. Use a limiter or keep headroom.
Pitch stays fixed on the boom; the movement comes from level, pan and the comb resonance, so it suits Matt's steady-pitch taste.

Polyrhythm Studio / Web Audio mapping: build the hit from OscillatorNode + noise buffer with fast gain/filter envelopes, BiquadFilterNode (lowpass/highpass), ConvolverNode reverb, DelayNode per channel via ChannelSplitter for L/R offsets, GainNode tremolo driven by an envelope-scaled LFO.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Play the hit lower on the keyboard so it sounds less like a tom. Reshape the body with filter-envelope decay, cutoff, resonance and noise amount.
Add harmonic bass enhancement plus a sub oscillator one octave down (two octaves only if needed). Move the low-cut EQ from about 83 Hz down to about 50 Hz and steepen it from 24 to 36 dB/oct.
steps.expect: Much more body and sub without uncontrolled rumble below 50 Hz

steps.action: Remove any attack/snap boost band and replace it with a gentle 6 dB/oct low-pass.
steps.expect: High-end snap gone; it now reads as far away and rumbling

steps.action: Reverb: low-cut the reverb itself at about 100 Hz with a 24 dB/oct slope (by ear), choose a large impulse and set the mix to about 40%.
steps.expect: Big low explosion tail that does not swamp the low end

steps.action: Optional: add a tempo-synced quarter-note delay with resonance off, high-pass the delay at about 90 Hz and low-pass it at about 4 kHz, and lower its level. Offset the left repeat about 7.3 ms early and the right about 7.3 ms late.
steps.expect: Echo sounds like the hall answering, spread in stereo

steps.action: Optional parallel tail: split the signal after the reverb into a parallel lane with a tremolo (rectangle, eighth notes, depth up, blend about 50%). Drive the tremolo depth with an envelope: delay about 140 ms, decay about 2 s (match the reverb length), sustain 0.
steps.expect: The first transient is clean, then the tail chops and fades out

steps.action: Alternative tail: replace the tremolo with a quarter-note auto-pan using the same envelope on depth, or put distortion or other modulation on the parallel lane.
steps.expect: Tail moves across the stereo field after the hit

steps.action: Optional modern 'deep metal' drop: add a comb filter on the lane, tuned low, about 14-40 Hz (12 Hz is too low), with feedback about 50% and max frequency reduced to tame the highs. Blend it with the split ratio, and you can add the delay after it.
steps.expect: Dark metallic, spring-like resonance under the boom, as in trailer drops

verification: Spectrum shows energy extending to about 50 Hz with little content above a few kHz (6 dB/oct roll-off audible).
Reverb return has almost nothing below about 100 Hz.
The tremolo/auto-pan depth is zero at the transient and rises after about 140 ms, then fades with the reverb.
There is no clipping on the master after sub, delay and comb are added.
